picks.rationale: This is the largest effect size on the board: HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.25-0.45) in HRD-positive disease, and HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.28-0.66) in the BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive subgroup that mirrors this patient, against the all-comer niraparib HR of 0.62. She is already on the bevacizumab backbone, so the only thing standing between her and the highest-upside maintenance regimen is one validated genomic-instability assay. I will champion ordering the Myriad MyChoice GIS now and committing to this regimen if it returns at least 42; below that threshold she is HRD-negative and this option closes. I am not pretending the eligibility is settled, only that the upside justifies forcing the GIS question instead of defaulting straight to niraparib.
primary_concerns: Eligibility is contingent on a GIS at least 42 she does not yet have; if it returns below 42 the regimen is foreclosed and the HR 0.33 never applies to her
Combination-arm grade 3+ AE near 57%, with grade 3+ hypertension 19% and anemia 17%, layered onto a patient with high VTE history and a prior IVC filter
Adds a PARP myelosuppression burden on top of bevacizumab's thrombotic and bleeding risk

picks.rationale: If the GIS comes back below 42, this is the bet I want: an all-comer label with no BRCA gate and no validated-score requirement, overall HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.50-0.76) and HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.31-0.59) in the HRD-positive stratum. The preclinical pharmacology is unusually specific to her tumor: niraparib partitions into tumor at 3.3x plasma and cut growth 58% in a BRCA-wild-type PDX where olaparib barely moved (pmid:30647846), and it ranks among the strongest PARP trappers tested (pmid:23066039). It is oral and low-burden, which fits her stated preference. My honest reservation is that thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% at grade 3+ press directly on her severe-myelosuppression veto, mitigated but not erased by individualized starting dose.
primary_concerns: Grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% sit on the patient's named severe-myelosuppression / febrile-neutropenia veto; individualized dosing reduces but does not remove this
Baseline WBC is already 3.5, a thin reserve for a myelosuppressive agent in a 70-79 age band
All-comer benefit is real but smaller than the HRD-positive-gated PAOLA-1 magnitude

picks.rationale: A second all-comer PARP maintenance with an ITT HR of 0.52 (95% CI 0.40-0.68) that held in the HRD-negative stratum, so a BRCA-wild-type tumor qualifies without a BRCA gate, exactly like niraparib. The reason it sits behind niraparib rather than beside it is that I have no tumor-partitioning or trapping pharmacology pointing rucaparib at this specific BRCA-proficient biology, where niraparib carries that preclinical argument. Grade 3+ anemia 28.7% and neutropenia 14.6% engage the same myelosuppression veto.
primary_concerns: Grade 3+ anemia 28.7% and neutropenia 14.6% trigger the severe-myelosuppression veto, as with niraparib
Rucaparib is the redundant second all-comer PARP; its marginal edge over niraparib rests on board agreement rather than distinct biology
No biology-specific preclinical edge over niraparib in this BRCA-wild-type setting, so it is the redundant PARP rather than the lead one

picks.rationale: She is already on this and already at R0, and the OVATION 2 topline reads HR 0.79 for PFS (14.9 vs 11.9 mo) and HR 0.69 for OS, an OS signal large enough that I will not wave it off as a backbone afterthought. It works through the peritoneal immune microenvironment rather than the MSI/TMB checkpoint axis her MSS, TMB-low tumor forecloses, so the usual immunotherapy disqualifier does not apply here. The honest weaknesses are that this is early-phase data from a sponsor topline with CIs not reported and no peer-reviewed per-term safety table, and the magnitude trails the PARP options. I rank it as the clean continuation play: no veto triggered, IP delivery generally well tolerated, and it keeps a credible OS hypothesis alive while the GIS result decides the PARP question.
primary_concerns: Efficacy rests on a sponsor topline and a 2025 abstract; CIs are unreported and no peer-reviewed grade 3+ safety table is yet public
Smaller PFS effect than the PARP maintenance options, and the OS estimate is immature
Investigational status means access and continuity outside the trial structure are not guaranteed

notes: Risktaker ordering: I lead with the highest-magnitude option (PAOLA-1 olaparib+bev, HRD-positive HR 0.33) made contingent on forcing the MyChoice GIS, because she is already on bevacizumab and the only barrier is one assay. Niraparib is my fallback the moment the GIS reads below 42, and it carries the only tumor-specific preclinical pharmacology (Sun 2018 partitioning, Murai trapping) in a BRCA-wild-type tumor. Rucaparib is the redundant all-comer PARP (ITT HR 0.52). GEN-1 is the no-veto continuation with a real but immature OS signal. I did not rank letrozole (single ER-positive, PR-negative endocrine signal, serious-RoB retrospective evidence, magnitude too small for a rank-1-leaning persona to champion) or the PI3K/MAP2K4 phase-1 baskets (no validated benefit for amplification or MAP2K4 loss, no approved matched agent). SOLO1 olaparib monotherapy is foreclosed by BRCA-wild-type and is correctly excluded. The PARP picks all press on the severe-myelosuppression veto; I keep them because the maintenance benefit is large, but I flag the veto tension honestly rather than papering over it.

picks.rationale: I put bevacizumab first because it is the option whose safety I can actually predict: approved since 2014, two large 1L phase-3 trials (GOG-218 n=1873, ICON7 n=1528) with more than a decade of post-marketing follow-up, and the patient is already on it and tolerating it. Neither named veto is triggered. The grade 2+ hypertension rate (22.9% vs 7.2% in GOG-218) has a well-worn management algorithm, and bowel-wall disruption stayed at 2.6%. My one real caution is VTE/bleeding given her high VTE history and prior IVC filter, so I would keep her on the established BP and bleeding monitoring rather than escalate.
primary_concerns: VTE and bleeding risk against the patient's high VTE history and prior IVC filter, though no neuropathy or myelosuppression veto applies
PFS benefit only; OS was not improved in the GOG-218 overall population and the ICON7 OS gain was confined to the high-risk subset

picks.rationale: Niraparib is the strongest efficacy fit on paper: PRIMA (n=733) enrolled all-comers with no BRCA mutation or validated HRD score required, HR 0.62 overall, and it is FDA-approved on-label, so a BRCA-WT genomically-unstable tumor qualifies cleanly. I rank it second rather than first only because it trips her stated severe-myelosuppression veto head-on: grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7%, anemia 31%, neutropenia 12.8%. The individualized starting dose by body weight and baseline platelet count blunts that risk but does not erase it, and her baseline WBC is already 3.5. I can be talked up to rank 1 if a hematology-supported dose plan and a clear cytopenia-management pathway are documented.
primary_concerns: Triggers the patient's severe myelosuppression / febrile neutropenia veto: grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7%, anemia 31%
Baseline WBC 3.5 narrows the marrow reserve before any drug-related cytopenia

picks.rationale: Letrozole is the gentlest option in front of the board: oral, once-daily, no infusion burden, and it trips none of her vetoes, which suits the 70-79 age band and her oral-therapy preference. The catch is the evidence base. The supporting data are a non-randomized retrospective comparison nested in a translational ER-expression study (ROBINS-I serious), and her PR-negativity predicts a more modest response than the ER-positive (~80% nuclei) reading alone suggests. I keep it on the list as a low-toxicity add-on or later-line choice, not as a substitute for a maintenance regimen with randomized backing. Arthralgia and bone-density loss on prolonged aromatase inhibition are the main things to watch.
primary_concerns: Evidence is a non-randomized retrospective series (ROBINS-I serious), not the randomized data the higher-ranked options carry
PR-negativity tempers the expected endocrine magnitude despite ~80% ER positivity

notes: Ranking is deliberately tolerability-first. The single most decision-relevant workup remains a validated genomic-instability score (Myriad MyChoice CDx GIS >=42 or FDA equivalent): if it comes back >=42 the patient becomes PAOLA-1 eligible and olaparib + bevacizumab (HR 0.33 HRD-positive; 0.43 in the BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive subgroup) moves into contention, though I would weigh that combination's ~57% grade 3+ AE rate and added hypertension against her VTE history before endorsing it. Below 42 she is HRD-negative and the all-comer PARP question stays with niraparib. I did not rank the early-phase PI3K or MAP2K4 baskets or GEN-1; they sit outside a conservative round-1 pick on safety-characterization grounds, and SOLO1 olaparib monotherapy is foreclosed by BRCA-WT status.

picks.rationale: PRIMA is the one row that does what I want a maintenance decision to rest on: a registered phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (n=733) that enrolled all-comers and hit its primary PFS endpoint with no BRCA gate and no validated HRD score required (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.50-0.76, p<0.001). For a BRCA wild-type tumor with only a qualitative instability call, that all-comer enrollment is the eligibility match itself, not a cross-stratum extrapolation. RoB2 reads low. The real cost is hematologic, and it lands on a named veto.
primary_concerns: Toxicity, not bias: grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% trip the patient's severe-myelosuppression veto, only partly blunted by individualized starting dose.

The headline HR 0.62 is the overall population; the larger HRD-positive effect (HR 0.43) does not apply to a BRCA wild-type tumor without a validated score, so set expectations off the all-comer estimate.
OS was immature at the primary report (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.44-1.11), so the durable benefit is PFS, not a demonstrated survival gain.

picks.rationale: ATHENA-MONO replicates the PRIMA signal in a separate phase 3 (n=538), and the benefit holds in the intent-to-treat population rather than resting on the BRCA-mutant stratum. Replication across two independent trials is what raises my confidence in the all-comer PARP-maintenance rationale for this tumor. I rank it second only because the case already carries a bevacizumab backbone and PRIMA is the larger, label-defining all-comer dataset.
primary_concerns: Effect size is the primary JCO ITT HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.40-0.68, pmid 35658487); rucaparib and niraparib are near-interchangeable all-comer PARPs.
Same severe-myelosuppression veto applies: grade 3+ anemia 28.7%, neutropenia 14.6%, plus grade 3+ ALT/AST elevation 10.6% (usually transient, baseline LFTs normal here).
AE-related discontinuation ran 11.8%, which matters for a maintenance commitment in the 70-79 band.

picks.rationale: PAOLA-1 carries the largest effect on the table (HR 0.33), but that estimate is the HRD-positive subgroup, and the BRCA wild-type analogue closest to this patient is a further-nested subgroup at HR 0.43. The trial design is sound (RoB2 low), but eligibility is the problem: PAOLA-1 defines HRD-positive by MyChoice GIS >=42 or tumor BRCA, and Altera's qualitative instability call does not clear that companion-diagnostic bar. I will not rank a subgroup-gated option above a primary-endpoint all-comer result while the gating assay is still pending.
primary_concerns: The load-bearing HR 0.33 is a predefined subgroup estimate, not the ITT result; the ITT HR was 0.59 (95% CI 0.49-0.72), a materially smaller effect.
Eligibility is contingent on a validated GIS the patient does not have; rank can move up only if MyChoice returns >=42.
Combination-arm grade 3+ AE near 57% with grade 3+ hypertension 19%, which compounds the patient's VTE history and prior IVC filter.

notes: Ranked only the three options carrying registered phase 3 RCT evidence with a primary endpoint hit. bevacizumab (GOG-218 HR 0.717, PFS only, no overall-population OS benefit; ICON7 open-label, RoB2:Some, OS confined to a high-risk subgroup) is a defensible maintenance axis the patient is already on, but its evidence is PFS-grade and I would not elevate it over the PARP options on quality. The rest do not meet my bar: letrozole rests on a non-randomized retrospective comparison nested in a translational paper (ROBINS-I:Serious, tier 4), GEN-1/IMNN-001 is early-phase with efficacy only from sponsor topline and a 2025 abstract (no per-term AE table, RoB2:Some), and the PIK3CA/MAP2K4 baskets are phase-1 trial-matching tags with no efficacy estimand. I did not read case/<slug>/clinical/ per instructions. SOLO1 (olaparib monotherapy) is correctly foreclosed by BRCA wild-type and is not an option.

picks.rationale: NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 lists single-agent PARP maintenance after a 1L platinum response as a category 2A option for all-comers, and PRIMA enrolled without requiring a BRCA mutation or a validated HRD score. That all-comer footing is what a BRCA wild-type, genomically unstable tumor needs, and the regimen is oral, which suits the patient's stated preference. ESMO endorses 1L PARP maintenance in this setting as well, so the cross-society read is consistent. The honest cost is myelosuppression, which sits on her toxicity veto list, though the individualized starting dose in PRIMA cut the grade 3+ thrombocytopenia rate.
primary_concerns: Triggers her severe-myelosuppression veto: grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% in PRIMA, needing platelet-based starting dose and close counts
Guideline benefit is largest in the HRD-positive stratum; in the BRCA wild-type, HRD-unquantified setting the all-comer estimate is the relevant one and it is smaller

picks.rationale: PAOLA-1 is the category 1 NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 maintenance option for HRD-positive disease and carries an ESMO-MCBS score, so on guideline grounds this is the highest-tier choice if she qualifies. The catch is the gate: NCCN ties the indication to HRD-positive status defined by tumor BRCA or a validated GIS at or above 42, and Altera's qualitative instability call does not meet that companion-diagnostic bar. She is already on the bevacizumab backbone, which makes the add-on operationally clean. I rank it second only because eligibility hinges on a MyChoice CDx score she does not yet have; send the assay and the rank reorders if it comes back at 42 or higher.
primary_concerns: Off the guideline-endorsed population until a validated GIS confirms HRD-positive; below 42 she defaults to all-comer niraparib
Bevacizumab VTE and bleeding risk is live given her high VTE history and prior IVC filter; combination-arm grade 3+ hypertension was 19%

picks.rationale: NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 lists bevacizumab maintenance as a category 2A all-comer option after 1L platinum, anchored by GOG-218 and ICON7, and she is already receiving it. ICON7 puts the largest gain in the high-risk subset, and a stage IIIc R0 patient sits adjacent to that group. Continuing it costs nothing in new decision-making and keeps a guideline-backed axis running while the GIS result decides whether olaparib gets layered on. The benefit is PFS, not OS, in the overall population, so I would not oversell it.
primary_concerns: VTE, bleeding, and hypertension class risk is the operative caution given her VTE history and IVC filter, even though no neuropathy or myelosuppression veto is triggered
Overall-population benefit is PFS-only; OS was not improved in GOG-218 and the ICON7 OS gain was confined to the high-risk subset

picks.rationale: ATHENA-MONO supports rucaparib as another all-comer 1L PARP maintenance option, with benefit holding in the intent-to-treat population that includes the BRCA wild-type stratum, so she qualifies without a BRCA gate. NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 carries the same single-agent PARP maintenance category 2A recommendation that covers this agent. I place it below niraparib mainly on label and prescribing familiarity in the 1L all-comer setting rather than any efficacy gap. Her baseline LFTs are normal, which helps with rucaparib's transaminase signal.
primary_concerns: Same severe-myelosuppression veto applies: grade 3+ anemia 28.7% and neutropenia 14.6%
Effect size confirmed as the primary JCO ITT HR 0.52 (pmid 35658487)

picks.rationale: NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 includes aromatase inhibitors among hormone-therapy options for recurrent or maintenance ER-positive disease, and her tumor is ER-positive in roughly 80% of nuclei. Letrozole is oral and low-burden, which fits her age band and preference, and none of her toxicity vetoes apply. PR-negativity predicts a tempered response, and the supporting evidence here is a non-randomized retrospective comparison rather than a randomized trial, so I rank it as a low-toxicity later-line or adjunct option rather than the primary maintenance choice. The guideline category for endocrine therapy is softer than the 2A PARP and bevacizumab recommendations above.
primary_concerns: ER-positive but PR-negative, which tempers the expected endocrine magnitude
Supporting data are retrospective and non-randomized (ROBINS-I serious), a weaker evidence base than the PARP and bevacizumab options

notes: Ranking is anchored to NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 categories. The cleanest guideline fit is all-comer 1L PARP maintenance (niraparib, PRIMA), which needs neither a BRCA mutation nor a validated HRD score, so it carries no contingency for this BRCA wild-type tumor. PAOLA-1 is the higher-tier category 1 regimen but is gated on a validated GIS the Altera qualitative call does not provide; the shared rank-1 workup the board should agree on is sending a MyChoice CDx (or FDA-equivalent) score, since a result at or above 42 promotes olaparib + bevacizumab over niraparib. SOLO1 (olaparib monotherapy) is foreclosed by BRCA wild-type status and is not ranked. GEN-1/IMNN-001 is the on-study investigational regimen she received and matters for board context, but it is not guideline-endorsed maintenance, so I leave it off the ranked list. The PIK3CA and MAP2K4 baskets are investigational-only with no approved matched therapy and no guideline standing; off-list for this persona.

picks.rationale: Bevacizumab is the one maintenance option that clears both of her vetoes outright: no added neuropathy, no severe myelosuppression. She is already on it, so this continues a backbone she tolerates rather than starting something new. The real cost is a caution rather than a veto: anti-angiogenic VTE and bleeding risk matters given her high VTE history and prior IVC filter, and it needs active management. The efficacy is PFS-only (GOG-218 HR 0.717) with no overall-survival gain, but for a woman in her seventies who folded tolerability into a 0.7 efficacy weight, a regimen she already tolerates beats a stronger one that trips a veto.
primary_concerns: Satisfies both vetoes: no neuropathy, no myelosuppression.
In tension with the thrombotic/bleeding-caution modality constraint (VTE history, IVC filter).
Modest efficacy ceiling: PFS only, no overall-survival signal.

picks.intervention_label: Validated genomic-instability score before olaparib + bevacizumab (PAOLA-1) eligibility
picks.rationale: Her own preferences name the validated GIS as the rank-1 shared workup, and it is the single test that decides whether the highest-magnitude PARP option is even on the table for her. A MyChoice GIS of at least 42 opens PAOLA-1 olaparib plus bevacizumab in the BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive subgroup (HR 0.43); below 42 she is HRD-negative, and I am not putting her through that combination's stacked myelosuppression and bleeding risk for a smaller return. It runs on archival FFPE in two to three weeks with no new procedure. Resolve the gate before we commit her to a maintenance intensity.
primary_concerns: Decision-gating workup, not a therapy, so it scores on decision-value rather than efficacy or toxicity.
Directly serves the patient's stated rank-1 preference.
Turnaround pushes the maintenance decision back a few weeks.

picks.rationale: Letrozole is the lowest-toxicity oral option in front of the board and it trips none of her vetoes, which is what the oral, low-infusion-burden preference is asking for: nothing added to the neuropathy or myelosuppression columns. The catch is the evidence. It rests on a non-randomized retrospective comparison, and she is ER-positive but PR-negative, so I expect a real but tempered signal rather than a PARP-sized one. It ranks here as the tolerability floor she can fall back to if the GIS comes back HRD-negative and she wants to stay off cytopenia-inducing maintenance.
primary_concerns: Clears every veto and the oral-preference constraint cleanly.
Weak, non-randomized evidence; PR-negativity predicts a tempered response.
Efficacy magnitude well below the PARP options.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib + bevacizumab (PAOLA-1, contingent on validated HRD-positive)
picks.rationale: This is the highest-magnitude maintenance on the board (HRD-positive HR 0.33; BRCA-non-mutated HRD-positive HR 0.43), and she is already on the bevacizumab half. I rank it low for her specifically because it is contingent and it stacks two of her concerns at once: eligibility needs a validated GIS of at least 42 she does not have, and the combination carries PARP myelosuppression on top of bevacizumab bleeding and VTE risk against her IVC-filter history. If the pick-2 GIS confirms HRD-positive, this jumps up the list. Until then it is a conditional option, not a recommendation I can make.
primary_concerns: Conditional on the pick-2 GIS result.
Stacks the myelosuppression veto and the VTE/bleeding caution.
Strongest efficacy only if HRD-positive is confirmed.

picks.rationale: She prefers trials and she is already on this one, the regimen that carried her to R0, so continuity is the argument here. It works through the immune microenvironment rather than the MSS/TMB-low checkpoint axis that is foreclosed for her, and intraperitoneal delivery has not tripped a veto so far. It stays mid-pack because the efficacy is still immature (ITT PFS HR 0.79, OS HR 0.69 on sponsor topline) and the infusion route is not the oral low-burden she would otherwise pick.
primary_concerns: Honors the prefers-trials preference and continues a tolerated regimen.
Investigational with immature efficacy; intraperitoneal delivery rather than oral.
No named veto triggered to date.

notes: Sharp tension this round between the 0.7 efficacy lean and the severe-myelosuppression veto. The cleanest all-comer PARP fits for a BRCA-WT, genomically-unstable tumor (niraparib PRIMA grade 3+ anemia 31% / thrombocytopenia 29%; rucaparib ATHENA-MONO grade 3+ anemia 29%) both hit her myelosuppression veto head-on, so I cannot lead with either despite the efficacy weight; if she chose to accept that risk with growth-factor and platelet support they would move up, but the veto is hers to lift, not mine. I led with bevacizumab because it is the only maintenance that clears both vetoes and she already tolerates it, and put the validated GIS at rank 2 because her free-text names it as the rank-1 workup and it gates the one high-magnitude option (PAOLA-1) that her bevacizumab backbone already half-sets-up. olaparib monotherapy / SOLO1 is foreclosed (BRCA WT) and is not ranked. The PI3K and MAP2K4 baskets are investigational-only with no validated benefit for amplification or MAP2K4 loss and do not fit her oral-preferred, efficacy-leaning profile better than the ranked options, so I left them off.
